Well, the duper's delight is quite apparent, so excusing that is not really the point.

Even so, context matters and it's important to get the full picture on things. Deception by omission is easy to debunk and taints any valid points in proximity.

Here, for example, the "that" in "that will get attention, this time" appears to refer to "the next one" in this short clip, creating an ominous and threatening implication. But, in the full context, it's just as likely to refer to "the testing was ramped up" or"nursing homes, getting factories ready, the testing regime".

The grin is creepy in any case. And someone who saw the full context would still think so. However, someone who is first shown this short clip, and then the full context, is likely to conclude that they've been tricked, and therefore dismiss the whole thing. Especially if they've shared the short clip, and were then "proven wrong" and embarrassed with the full context.

The solution is quite simple: Never take things out of context, and never accept anything that is missing context.
